x: Our readers will be sorry to learn of the indisposition of Ted Saunders, a Vice-Captain and prominent walker for many years past. All Belgravians will wish him a speedy recovery to normal health, and we all hope to see him fit and well in our company in the near future.

Of our other one-time invalids, Ted Saunders is out walking with us again, and Harry Shields has made a marvellously quick recovery from his recent operation, and will probably be running again over the country before you read these notes.
Roberts, competing in his first big race for us, was 44th, Harley 57th and Ted Saunders 68th. Frank Elson was compelled to retire from the race.
Reeve, is in the R.A.O.C.; whilst Ted Saunders is a corporal in an R.A.M.C. unit functioning in the Near East.

Len Fletcher and Frank Elson have assisted the Club in seven of these eight wins; Tommy Green six times; Fred Rickards on three occasions; Harold King, Frank Thorn and Ted Saunders each twice; and Joe King and Jack Field once each.
